notable_absence.finding: backup:native-cloud-integration is promoted as 'An Enterprise Edition feature'. This page documents the identical capability (cloud_credential_name, cloud_staging_dir, cloud_credentials_id/key, cloud_region, cloud_endpoint, cloud_force_path_style) with no Enterprise Edition statement anywhere on the page. Same open question as backup-create-and-edit-plans.json's MERGE-task finding: either the edition gate is real and undocumented on the REST reference, or the REST surface genuinely lifts the restriction, and the page does not let a reader tell which.

cross_component_finding: ROUND 11's FINDING HOLDS UP, AND THIS PAGE IS THE CLEANEST CONFIRMATION YET. The question this round was asked to check: is backup:repository 'the SAME construct whether it is written to by the cbbackupmgr CLI directly or by the Backup Service's own plan mechanism'? This page's repository-definition schema settles it at the field level, not just the label level. Its `archive` parameter is defined as 'a location on a filesystem, or on a cloud, that is not used for any other repository' - the exact same archive/repository containment relationship (backup:archive hasInternalComponent backup:repository) already promoted from cbbackupmgr's own config sub-command and tutorial pages, right down to the same filesystem-permission caveat: this page tells a non-root installer to 'use the `chgrp` command to set the group ID of the folder to `couchbase`', which is the identical instruction pattern cbbackupmgr's own docs give for the same archive directory. The `bucket_name` restriction ('If the bucket-name is provided, only data for this bucket is backed up... If no bucket-name is provided, data for all buckets on the cluster is backed up') matches cbbackupmgr's own --include-data bucket scoping semantics in shape, though this page does not use that flag name. SECOND, EXTENDING THE FINDING RATHER THAN JUST CONFIRMING IT: the round's prompt asked specifically about the cloud angle, and this page is where that shows up - its Cloud-Specific Parameters sub-section (cloud_credential_name, cloud_staging_dir, cloud_credentials_id, cloud_credentials_key, cloud_region, cloud_endpoint, cloud_force_path_style) is the REST expression of backup:native-cloud-integration, previously known only from the CLI side. Reused rather than forked into a REST-specific concept, on the same logic as backup:repository itself. THIRD, A NARROWING WORTH FLAGGING RATHER THAN SMOOTHING OVER: cbbackupmgr's native-cloud-integration is documented as covering FOUR providers (object-store:aws-s3/azure-blob-storage/gcp-storage/azure-data-lake-storage-gen2). This page's own parameter descriptions read as narrower or at least AWS-first in their illustrative detail - `cloud_credentials_id` is glossed 'For AWS, this is the _access key id_', `cloud_credentials_key` 'For AWS, this is the _AWS secret access key_', and `cloud_force_path_style` is scoped explicitly to 'S3 or S3 compatible storages'. Azure and GCP are never named on this page at all. I have not concluded the REST surface is AWS/S3-only from this alone (the parameter names themselves - cloud_credential_name, cloud_region - read as provider-agnostic), but the asymmetry in which provider gets the illustrative detail is real and worth a follow-up read of the sibling batch's backup-manage-config.md or backup-node-threads.md if either touches cloud credentials again.
